name: Large-format porcelain tiles
region: Sassuolo and Castellón, with a global market
summary: Very hard, dense tiles that a factory presses in sizes of 60 by 60 cm and above, up to slabs of 3 m. A digital printer gives the surface the look of stone, wood or concrete. Fine joints make the wall or floor read as one skin.

philosophy.core_thesis: One large, dense, thin sheet of ceramic makes a seamless surface that holds the look of another material.
design_principles: Press the tile to 60 by 60 cm or more, and up to 120 by 280 cm or 160 by 320 cm for a slab.
Fire the body to less than 0.5 per cent water absorption, so that it takes frost, stain and wear.
Keep the tile thin, 6 to 12 mm, for a wall, and 20 mm for an outdoor floor.
Print the surface by inkjet with a design from stone, wood, concrete or metal, and vary the image over many slabs.
Rectify the edges and set the joints to 1 to 2 mm, so that the surface reads as one sheet.
Choose a matt or satin surface of 5 to 30 GU, and add a texture that follows the print.
Use the slab for floors, walls, worktops and facades in one material, with no change at the corner.
Plan the cut and the layout in advance, because a slab has a high cost of break.
anti_patterns: A small tile with a wide joint and a hand-made edge
A glossy mirror-like glaze that shows each footprint
A single print that repeats on every tile
A thick, soft body that absorbs water

form.shape: Large square and rectangular floor and wall tiles, thin slabs, worktop slabs, skirting and step pieces.
form.profile: A flat, rectified face with sharp or slightly softened arrises; a printed texture follows the image.
form.foot_and_rim: The back has a fine grid for adhesive; the edge is cut true and may carry a small chamfer.
form.proportion: Common sizes are 60 by 60 cm, 60 by 120 cm and 120 by 240 cm; the thickness is 6 to 20 mm.
rules: Cut the edge true to within 0.5 mm.
Print each slab with a different part of the source image.
Match the grout colour to the tile and keep the joint under 2 mm.

bodies.rule: Use a porcelain stoneware of fine feldspathic clay, pressed at high pressure and fired dense. Keep porous earthenware out.

methods: pressing the powder in a large hydraulic press or by continuous compaction
printing the surface by digital inkjet
grinding and rectifying the edge after firing
forming.joins: Slabs are bonded to the base with a thin adhesive, and the joints are 1 to 2 mm.
forming.details: A rectified edge, a print that repeats only over many slabs, a fine surface texture and a back with a grid.

glaze.pattern: A digital image of stone, wood or concrete, with veins that run across slabs, under a thin matt or satin layer.
glaze.gloss: Matt or satin, 5 to 30 GU; a polished face can reach 70 GU.
glaze.wear: The body is very hard and does not stain or freeze; a polished face scratches and the print sits in the top layer.

palette.strategy: Neutral stone, concrete and wood tones; colour comes from the image and not from the glaze.

firing.kiln: A continuous roller kiln of 100 m or more, fired by gas.
processes: firing in a roller kiln for 40 to 60 minutes
firing.scale: A line produces several thousand square metres in a day, and a factory prints each slab by inkjet.
firing.signs: A uniform body, a rectified edge, a print with no repeat in a short run and a fine grid on the back.

pieces.form: Tile of 60 by 120 cm with a concrete print and a satin surface
Slab of 120 by 240 cm with a marble print that runs across 2 slabs
Tile of 20 by 120 cm with a wood print and a matt texture
Through-body tile of 60 by 60 cm with a plain surface
Tile with a screen-printed fine pattern on a matt body

evidence.title: Porcelain stoneware floor tile, 17 by 17 cm

emotion.target_response: A calm, large and silent surface: the viewer sees a wall that seems to have no seams.

use_cases: a modern floor or wall with a stone or concrete look
a worktop or facade in thin ceramic
a minimal interior with few joints
avoid_when: the brief needs a hand-made or irregular tile
the brief needs a glossy glazed colour
the brief needs a historic look

modifiers.how: Cut the format to 7.5 by 15 cm, add a high gloss glaze and a bevel, and lay in a brick bond.
Use a small tile with an uneven glaze, a wide joint and a deep, shimmering colour.
